newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Captured Philippine suspect not rebel head -report.
newsitem.headline: Captured Philippine suspect not rebel head -report.

text.p: A Philippine armed forces report released on Saturday said that police captured six suspected members of a Moslem rebel group but apparently not its leader as earlier reported.

Armed Forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera earlier told reporters he was informed that government agents had captured Abdurajak Janjalani, the leader of the Moslem fundamentalist group Abu Sayyaf. Acedera said he had yet to see the formal report.

The internal report, made public by the armed forces, said that of the six suspected Abu Sayyaf members arrested in the central island of Cebu, one was a 21 year-old named Jimar Manatad Abubakar using the alias Khadaffy Janjalani.
The elusive Abdurajak Janjalani has been described by Moslem politicians to be in his late 20s or early 30s.
In the past, there have been instances when the military announced the arrest of a rebel leader only to renege later after realising it was a case of mistaken identity.
It was not immediately clear why General Acedera said earlier on Saturday the captured guerrilla was the head of the Abu Sayyaf.
The Abu Sayyaf has been pushing for an Islamic state on the southern island of Mindanao in the Philippines. The military has blamed the group for a wave of kidnappings and bombings in the south.
Janjalani has been the object of a massive manhunt for several years, with a 1.5 million peso ($57,000) price on his head. ($1 = 26 pesos)
